summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with fevers, rigors, and worsening cough and dyspnea following a presumed upper respiratory infection. He was found to have a retrocardial opacity on chest X-ray concerning for early pneumonia, leukocytosis, and hypotension on arrival. He received IV fluids and antibiotics in the emergency department and was admitted for further management. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and had resolving leukocytosis by hospital day 3. His chronic conditions—including hypertension, aortic stenosis, and SIADH-related hyponatremia—were stable and managed without intervention. He was discharged home on a short course of oral levofloxacin with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.
